skill.name: dast-nuclei
skill.description: Guide authorized Nuclei vulnerability scans across web applications, APIs, and infrastructure, including authentication, custom templates, CI integration, triage, and reporting.
skill.summary: Plan, run, validate, and report authorized Nuclei vulnerability scans.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholder URLs, defensive examples, and detection-rule literals. Confirmed risks include remote pipe-to-shell execution, token access by mutable CI actions, sensitive credential extraction, unrestricted targets, and command-line secret exposure. No prompt injection, obfuscation, or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The CI template pipes a script from a mutable remote branch directly into Bash.
remediation.suggestion: Download a versioned release, verify its checksum or signature, inspect it, and execute the verified local file.

remediation.issue: Third-party GitHub Actions use mutable branches or version tags while receiving repository context or secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every action to an audited full commit SHA and use a controlled dependency update process.

remediation.issue: The manual workflow accepts an unrestricted scan target.
remediation.suggestion: Validate targets against an approved allowlist and reject private, link-local, metadata, and out-of-scope addresses.

remediation.issue: Authenticated examples expand credentials into command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use a restricted secret or configuration mechanism, disable command tracing, mask logs, and rotate any exposed credentials.

remediation.issue: The custom template can retrieve and extract credentials from exposed environment files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit opt-in, redact extracted values, restrict result access, and avoid retaining raw response bodies.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Workflow Scan Target
semantic_findings.description: The manual workflow accepts any target URL and passes it directly to Nuclei. An authorized workflow user could scan unapproved external or runner-reachable internal services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The target_url workflow input is required and is consumed without an allowlist or network-range validation.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Third-Party CI Actions
semantic_findings.description: Executable workflow templates reference third-party actions through mutable branches or tags. Upstream compromise or retagging could execute changed code with repository context and secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files visibly use references including @main, @master, @v1, and @v2 instead of immutable commit SHAs.

semantic_findings.title: Credentials Exposed in Command Arguments
semantic_findings.description: Authentication examples interpolate bearer tokens and session cookies into command-line headers. Expanded secrets can be exposed through process inspection, shell history, or verbose logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shell expands credential variables inside Nuclei header arguments, which are commonly visible in local process metadata and command traces.

content.value_statement: Known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations can escape manual review. This skill guides authorized Nuclei scans, template selection, validation, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Provides Nuclei commands for single targets, target lists, severity filters, tags, rate limits, and concurrency.
Guides authenticated scans with bearer tokens, cookies, API keys, OAuth, SAML, and MFA examples.
Supplies CI workflow templates for scheduled scans, artifact uploads, SARIF reporting, and notifications.
Explains custom HTTP, DNS, and network templates with matchers, extractors, workflows, and fuzzing.
Maps findings to OWASP Top 10 and CWE categories with verification and remediation guidance.
Provides false-positive triage methods using filters, stronger matchers, manual verification, and suppression records.
limitations: Nuclei must be installed separately, and the helper scripts cited by the documentation are not included.
Active scans can affect target availability and always require explicit authorization, scope controls, and suitable rate limits.
Automated findings require manual validation and do not prove exploitability or business impact.
Authenticated examples handle sensitive tokens that may appear in process arguments, logs, or scan results.

use_cases.title: Triage Application Exposure
use_cases.description: Run scoped CVE, OWASP, and misconfiguration checks, then validate important findings before remediation.

use_cases.title: Add CI Security Gates
use_cases.description: Configure scheduled or pull-request scans with severity thresholds, SARIF uploads, and retained artifacts.

use_cases.title: Develop Custom Checks
use_cases.description: Create focused Nuclei templates with constrained requests, precise matchers, extractors, and local test targets.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an authorized Nuclei scan for [target]. Use critical and high severities, a 25-request rate limit, and include validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Authenticated Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authorized scan for [application] using [authentication type]. Protect credentials, limit scope, and explain how to verify findings.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Nuclei CI workflow for [repository]. Pin dependencies, validate approved targets, upload SARIF, and fail only on verified policy thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Custom Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Specify a Nuclei template for [vulnerability pattern]. Minimize requests, avoid destructive payloads, use precise matchers, and define a false-positive test plan.

output_examples.input: Plan a critical and high severity scan of an authorized staging application at 25 requests per second.
output: Confirm the written scope and exclude third-party services.
Run only critical and high templates with conservative concurrency.
Store results in a restricted location and manually validate each important finding.

output_examples.input: Review a Nuclei report that claims a critical exposed administration panel.
output_examples.output: The review checks authentication, response content, affected version, and mitigating controls before assigning a final severity and remediation owner.

output_examples.input: Design a custom check for an exposed application configuration endpoint.
output_examples.output: The design uses a small request budget, status and content matchers, redacted evidence, a negative matcher, and an authorized local test case.

best_practices: Verify written authorization, target ownership, and exclusions before every scan.
Start with low request rates and concurrency, then monitor application health before increasing load.
Restrict scan results, redact credentials, and manually validate critical or high findings.
anti_patterns: Do not scan third-party, production, private, or link-local targets without explicit approval.
Do not place credentials in shared command histories, logs, templates, or unrestricted artifacts.
Do not treat an automated match as proof of exploitability or confirmed business impact.

faq.question: Does this skill install Nuclei?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but Nuclei and optional tools must be installed and trusted separately.

faq.question: Can it scan production systems?
faq.answer: Yes, only with explicit authorization, conservative limits, approved templates, monitoring, and a rollback or stop procedure.

faq.question: Does it support authenticated scanning?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents bearer tokens, cookies, API keys, OAuth, SAML, and MFA patterns.

faq.question: Can it create custom Nuclei templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains template structure, protocol types, matchers, extractors, workflows, payloads, testing, and validation.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: Reproduce the result, verify authentication and versions, inspect mitigating controls, refine matchers, and record justified suppressions.

faq.question: Are the referenced helper scripts included?
faq.answer: No. The current package contains documentation and YAML assets, but it does not contain the cited scripts directory.
